The *Paññattihāravibhaṅga* (Ne 14) is an analytical section of the *Nettippakaraṇa*, a post-canonical methodological treatise categorized within the late strata of the Pali Sutta collections [SuttaCentral]. It provides an exposition (*vibhaṅga*) of *paññatti-hāra*, the interpretive mode or conveyer dealing with designations, descriptions, and concepts. SuttaCentral records one modern-language translation of the text [SuttaCentral].
Cross-references compiled by SuttaCentral associate the text with prominent early discourses and parallels across traditions, notably the *Dhammacakkappavattanasutta* (SN 56.11; alongside its versions in the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* [Kd 1], the Tibetan *Dharma-cakra-pravartana-sūtra* [D 31], the *Lalitavistara* [Lal 26], and Chinese T 109 and T 1450.6), the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 1), the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 20.6), the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 2.6, Ps 2.7), and collections of the *Udānavarga* (UV 2; T 212.2; T 213.2) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, with 1,489 matching passages found across 93 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest corpora sharing textual material with the *Paññattihāravibhaṅga* include the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), the *Sacca Saṁyutta* (SN 56), the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 1.6), and the *Guhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 2), as well as commentary and subcommentary layers such as the *Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and *Nettivibhāvinī* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of this text with the Chinese *Madhyama-āgama* (T 26), *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125), and *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 100), as well as the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (D 326) and Prajñāpāramitā texts [DharmaNexus].
